title: Usage Guardrail: multi-tenant spike & regression detector for cost/latency
creator: Rhea Patel
description: Build a noise-resistant anomaly detection service that surfaces and alerts on rapid spikes or regressions in per-tenant usage, cost, and end-to-end latency. The service will integrate with the Console backend, subscribe to our streaming metrics pipeline (Kafka), and power both realtime alerts and daily RCA candidates in the Console UI.
background: Existing Console alerts rely on simple static thresholds and rule-based heuristics. These generate a high false positive rate for high-variance tenants and do not attribute root causes across pricing tiers, model variants, or routing fallbacks. Support and SRE spend time triaging noisy signals; customers miss regressions (e.g., billing spikes) because alerts were suppressed or ambiguous.
goals: Detect and route significant usage/cost/latency anomalies to the Console alerting engine within 2 minutes of onset for 95% of incidents
Reduce false positive alerts by >= 40% for top-100 tenants compared to current baseline
Provide structured attribution (model variant, region, plan tier, route) in each alert to speed triage
Expose a clear canary/rollout path and allow per-customer sensitivity tuning in Console
success_metrics: mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for Console-detected usage incidents decreases by 25%
false positive rate (FP) measured on historical annotated set falls >=40%
fraction of alerts with automatic attribution metadata >=80%
no more than 0.5% additional billing alerts misfired during canary on top-100 tenants
scope_in: Realtime detector in the console backend that consumes Kafka usage/cost/latency topics
Adaptive per-tenant baselining (seasonal + recent window) and confidence scoring
Attribution pipeline: join with model catalog, route metadata, pricing tier, dedicated vs hosted flags
Alert deduplication, severity assignment, and enrichment for Console UI and Slack/email notifications
Backfill job for scoring historical windows and building labeled FP dataset
scope_out: Full ML retraining infra for long-term model lifecycle management (will integrate later)
Automatic remediation (throttles/fallbacks) — only advisory alerts for MVP
Deep integration with billing invoice generation; we will provide attribution but not adjust invoices automatically
design_decisions: Use a hybrid approach: simple statistical detectors (robust z-score + EWMAs) for low-latency signal, complemented by a lightweight online ML classifier (logistic regression on engineered features) to reduce false positives.
Stream-first architecture: implement detection in Flink streaming jobs to minimize end-to-end time-to-detect; persist enriched events to usage_anomalies topic for downstream Console services.
Per-tenant thresholds will be derived from a rolling 28-day seasonal baseline with weekday/hour-of-day buckets to handle diurnal patterns.
Attribution will be best-effort joins using precomputed enrichment tables (materialized daily) to avoid high-cardinality joins in the hot path.
Alert severity mapping will include cost impact estimate (USD) calculated using per-token pricing snapshot at time of anomaly onset.
tradeoffs: Statistical detectors are simple and explainable but less adaptive to concept drift; ML classifiers reduce FP but require labeled data and monitoring for model drift.
Performing enrichment joins in the hot path would increase latency and cost; we instead emit minimally-enriched alerts then run an enrichment worker that updates Console with attribution within 30s.
Using Flink increases operational complexity vs. a pure batch scoring approach but meets the 2-minute detection SLA requirement.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (dev): unit tests + local Flink job with synthetic tenants; smoke test on staging Kafka topic
Phase 1 (canary): enable detection for internal + demo tenants (10 tenants) for 2 weeks; compare against human-labeled historical events
Phase 2 (expanded canary): top-100 customers enabled with conservative sensitivity for 1 week; monitor FP/TP metrics and cost estimates
Phase 3 (prod): global enable with per-tenant default sensitivity and UI toggle in Console; full alert delivery to Slack/email and Console inbox
Rollback: ability to pause stream processors and switch to passive scoring mode that writes diagnostics but does not emit alerts
monitoring: Processor lag (Kafka consumer offset), detection latency histogram, alerts emitted per minute
False positive ratio estimated from control set; precision/recall computed from labeled backfill
Enrichment success rate and attribution completeness percentage
Pipeline cost (estimated USD/day) for streaming jobs and enrichment workers
acceptance_criteria: Flink job deployed to prod cluster and processes live usage topic with <120s median detection latency
Console shows enriched alert cards with attribution fields (model, region, plan) for test tenants
Automated FP check on annotated backfill shows >=40% reduction vs baseline
Slack notifications include cost impact estimate and link to Console RCA card
Playbook document for SRE/Support created and reviewed (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/playbooks/pull/367)
